q: How was Paul made an apostle of Christ Jesus?
a: Paul was made an apostle by to the commandment of God.

q: Where did Paul urge Timothy to remain?
a: He urged Timothy to remain in Ephesus.

q: What was Timothy to command certain people not to do?
a: He was to command them not to teach differently.

q: What did Paul say was the goal of his commandment and teaching?
a: The goal of his commandment was love from a pure heart, from a good conscience, and from sincere faith.

q: For whom is the law made?
a: The law is for lawless, rebellious, ungodly people, and sinners.

q: What sins did Paul formerly commit?
a: Paul was a blasphemer, persecutor, and a violent man.

q: Who did Christ Jesus come into the world to save?
a: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners.

q: Why does Paul say God gave him mercy?
a: God gave Paul mercy so that Jesus could demonstrate his patience in Paul as an example.

q: What did Paul tell Timothy to do in accordance with the prophecies made about Timothy?
a: Paul tells Timothy to fight the good fight.

q: What happened to some who rejected their faith and their good conscience?
a: These people have shipwrecked regarding the faith.

q: What did Paul do for those men who had rejected faith and a good conscience and had shipwrecked their faith?
a: Paul gave them over to Satan so that they may be taught not to blaspheme.

q: For whom does Paul request that prayers be made?
a: Paul requests prayers be made for all people.

q: What kind of life does Paul desire Christians be allowed to live?
a: Paul desires that Christians be allowed to live a peaceful and quiet life in all godliness and dignity.

q: What is the position of Christ Jesus between God and man?
a: Christ Jesus is the one mediator between God and man.

q: What did Christ Jesus do for all?
a: Christ Jesus gave himself as a ransom for all.

q: Who does the apostle Paul teach?
a: Paul is a teacher of the Gentiles.

q: What does Paul want men to do?
a: Paul wants men to pray and lift up holy hands.

q: What does Paul want women to do?
a: Paul wants women to dress modestly and with self-control.

q: What does Paul not permit a woman to do?
a: Paul does not permit a woman to teach or to exercise authority over a man.

q: What is the first reason that Paul gives for not permitting a woman to teach or exercise authority over a man?
a: Paul’s first reason is that Adam was formed first.

q: What is the second reason that Paul gives for not permitting a woman to teach or exercise authority over a man?
a: Paul’s second reason is that Adam was not deceived, but the woman was deceived.

q: What kind of work is the work of an overseer?
a: The work of an overseer is good work.

q: What must an overseer be able to do?
a: An overseer must be able to teach.

q: How must an overseer handle alcohol and money?
a: An overseer must not be a drunkard, and must not love money.

q: How should an overseer’s children treat him?
a: An overseer’s children must obey and honor him.

q: Why is it important that an overseer manage his household well?
a: It is important because if he cannot manage his household well, he will likely not care well for a church.

q: What must an overseer’s reputation be with those outside the church?
a: An overseer must have a good reputation with those outside the church.

q: What should be done with deacons before they serve?
a: Before they serve, deacons should be tested.

q: What are some characteristics of godly women?
a: Godly women are dignified, not slanderers, sober, and trustworthy in everything.

q: What is the household of God?
a: The household of God is the church of the living God.

q: After Jesus appeared in the flesh, was justified by the Spirit, and was seen by angels, what happened?
a: Jesus was proclaimed among nations, believed in the world, and taken up in glory.

q: According to the Spirit, what will some people do in the later times?
a: Some people will leave the faith and attend to deceiving spirits and the teachings of demons.

q: In what does Paul tell Timothy to train himself?
a: Paul tells Timothy to train himself in godliness.

q: Why is training in godliness more profitable than bodily training?
a: Training in godliness is more profitable because it holds promise for this present life and the coming one.

q: What does Paul exhort Timothy to do with all of the good things that he has received in Paul’s teaching to him?
a: Paul exhorts Timothy to command and teach these things.

q: If Timothy continues faithfully in his life and teaching, who will be saved?
a: Timothy will save both himself and his listeners.

q: How did Paul tell Timothy to treat an older man in the church?
a: Paul told Timothy to exhort him as if he were a father.

q: What should children and grandchildren of a widow do for her?
a: Children and grandchildren should repay their parents and take care of her.

q: What has someone done who does not take care of those in his own household?
a: He has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.

q: For what should a widow be known?
a: A widow should be attested for good works.

q: Why should the church not enroll young widows onto the list of people for the church to care for?
a: These younger widows will later want to marry.

q: What does Paul want younger women to do?
a: Paul wants younger women to marry, to bear children, and to manage a household.

q: What should be done for elders who lead well?
a: Elders who lead well should be considered worthy of double honor.

q: Paul commands Timothy to be careful to keep these rules in what way?
a: Paul commands Timothy to be careful to keep these rules without favoritism.

q: When do the sins of people become known?
a: The sins of some people are evident, but the sins of others are not known until the judgment.

q: How did Paul say slaves should regard their masters?
a: Paul said that slaves should regard their masters as worthy of all honor.

q: What kind of person rejects healthy words and godly teaching?
a: The person who rejects healthy words and godly teaching is puffed up and understands nothing.

q: What does Paul say is great gain?
a: Paul says that godliness with contentment is great gain.

q: What did we bring into this world, and what can we take with us when we leave?
a: We have brought nothing into the world and cannot take anything out.

q: With what should we be content in this world?
a: We should be satisfied that we have food and clothing.

q: Into what do those who desire to become wealthy fall?
a: Those who desire to become wealthy fall into temptation and a trap.

q: What is a root of all kinds of evil?
a: The love of money is a root of all kinds of evil.

q: What has happened to some who have loved money?
a: Some who have loved money have been led away from the faith.

q: Where does God dwell?
a: God dwells in unapproachable light.

q: Why should the rich hope in God and not in uncertain riches?
a: The rich should hope in God because he provides us with everything that we enjoy.

q: Those who are rich in good works do what for themselves?
a: Those who are rich in good works store up for themselves a good foundation and grasp genuine life.

q: Finally, what does Paul tell Timothy to do with the things given to him?
a: Paul tells Timothy to guard what has been entrusted to him.
